verdict: Palantir's revenue jumped 48% to $1.0B — its first billion-dollar quarter — as U.S. commercial sales nearly doubled, and it kept $327M of that as profit.

segments.name: Government
segments.note: Software for governments, above all the U.S. military and intelligence agencies — up 49% YoY.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Software for companies — up 47% YoY, with U.S. commercial revenue up 93% to $306M as the AIP 'bootcamp' push kept winning customers.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and the 'bootcamp' try-before-you-buy push that has been winning commercial customers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platforms — Gotham, Foundry and the AIP AI layer.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company: legal, finance and offices.

otherDetail: Interest income of $56M and other income of $7M, net — shown as +$62M so the chart ties exactly to reported totals in whole $M.
footerNote: Net income here is the $327M attributable to common stockholders; total net income was $329M, with $2M belonging to noncontrolling interests. Segment figures are from Palantir's Q2 2025 10-Q, rounded to the nearest $M.

takeaways.title: U.S. business customers nearly doubled
takeaways.text: U.S. commercial revenue grew 93% YoY to $306M, and Palantir raised its outlook — it now expects full-year 2025 revenue of about $4.15B, with U.S. commercial growth of at least 85%.

takeaways.title: First billion-dollar quarter
takeaways.text: Total revenue reached $1,004M, up 48% YoY, with U.S. revenue up 68% to $733M — 73% of everything Palantir sells.

takeaways.title: Profit, not just growth
takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow was $569M — 57 cents of every revenue dollar — and GAAP net income attributable to shareholders was $327M, a 33% margin.
